The size comparison now uses int64 to prevent truncation. The flaw is in the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package and is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5020, https://go.dev/issue/79567, https://go.dev/cl/781663, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI). This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. The Go source tree it ships vendors a few golang.org/x/crypto packages for the standard library under /usr/lib/go/src/vendor, and its cmd tree vendors no golang.org/x/crypto package. In no published build is golang.org/x/crypto/ssh among them. Checked every published golang-1.26-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository (1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18, amd64 and arm64), together with the oci-config and debug-symbol (dbgsym) packages built from the same source: none contains a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh directory or source file, and no ELF file in them (including the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) contains the byte string golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, which every function name from that package would carry in a program's Go function table (pclntab). The golang-1.26-dev-fips-oci-config packages built from the same source in the DHI Debian security repository for Debian 13 hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog, and no program. The same byte search finds golang.org/x/net/html, an example import path in the help text of go list, in the go command of every published golang-1.26 and golang-1.26-dev package. It also finds golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, and the pclntab reader lists ssh.Dial, ssh.NewServerConn and (*channel).Write, in a test program built for linux/amd64 against golang.org/x/crypto v0.51.0 that calls them, so the search works. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/crypto/ssh takes it from its own golang.org/x/crypto requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/crypto in that program.
